aggregate_harm_screening.rationale: This review assesses the particular reported occurrence and its bounded consequences, including evidence-limited alleged consequences. Public reach does not establish lifecycle deployment. No model-wide audience or separate Aggregate Harm score is imported.

public_interpretation_before: ASIC describes human scammers using generative AI, deepfake endorsements, fabricated news, fake social proof and fake investment platforms to create materially false investment premises and induce economic transfers. The classifiable mechanism is AI-mediated deceptive economic solicitation, alongside requester-side identity-authority failure; autonomous AI manipulation and hidden generator control states remain unproved. The regulator’s deliberate public-figure image misuse supports requester-side identity-authority failure independently of the economic and social-engineering findings. Aggregate reported losses and takedowns remain distinct quantities, without attribution to every named portrayal. Static ads and human scripted calls do not establish an autonomous AI interlocutor. The independent dignity and autonomy assessment is Not aligned for the reported impersonation. Generator-specific controls are not established.

source_records_before.source_title: 26-195MR ASIC warns scammers are using AI to spin vast webs of deception
source_records_before.evidence_status_basis: ASIC's official media release directly establishes the regulator's observed rise in AI-assisted/deepfake investment scams, the campaign architecture it describes, the listed impersonated public figures, FY26 Scamwatch losses of A$7.4 million associated with those impersonations, and ASIC's takedown totals.

limitations: The release does not identify the synthetic-media models or vendors used by each scam.
The 19,400 takedowns include scam categories beyond AI-generated impersonation.
Scamwatch loss figures are report-based and may not capture every loss.

factual_basis_before: ASIC states that scammers are using generative AI to create networks of deepfake websites and endorsements, with fake news, fabricated comments, scripted calls and fake investment platforms reinforcing the deception. ASIC reports that the most-impersonated public figures in FY26 — including Alan Kohler, Anthony Albanese, Tom Piotrowski, Jacqui Lambie, Angus Taylor and others — were associated with A$7.4 million in reported Scamwatch losses. AIID Incident 1665 records a narrower example in which an AI-generated article falsely depicted Alan Kohler interviewing Reserve Bank Governor Michele Bullock to promote Boulder Sparhaven. The regulator describes multiple scam networks, not one continuous victim sequence. The loss total is not disaggregated by AI use; the takedown total covers phishing and other scam types as well. The reproduced Kohler/Bullock example has no separately established victim loss. Meta’s platform-wide detection claim does not establish its removal.
